claims: The Artemis II crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego on April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
The splashdown occurred in the Pacific Ocean near San Diego, California.
The splashdown occurred on Friday, April 10, 2026.
The splashdown occurred at 8:07 p.m. EDT / 5:07 p.m. PDT.
The Artemis II mission lasted 10 days.
The Artemis II mission launched on April 1 from Kennedy Space Center.
The Artemis II crew consisted of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The astronauts were recovered by the USS John P. Murtha.
Artemis II is the first crewed lunar mission in over 50 years.
The Orion capsule was named Integrity.
The Orion capsule slowed down from 25,000 mph to 20 mph before splashdown.
NASA and the U.S. Navy conducted the recovery operations.
